subject: BlueHarbor follow-up: comparative econ recap + proposed test matrix
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Schultz <emily.schultz@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: BlueHarbor follow-up: comparative econ recap + proposed test matrix

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap while it's fresh and a concrete next-steps proposal so your procurement and infra teams can see what we'd run.

Key takeaways from the demo call: 
- BlueHarbor primarily cares about steady-state per-1M token costs for high-concurrency customer-facing inference (chat + summarization).
- Main competitors on your shortlist are the public hyperscalers (HCS / P-Cloud) and a smaller inference API provider you cited (EdgeServe).
- Your current concerns: unpredictable per-token bills due to batching variability, and cache inefficiency on cold-starts for multi-tenant workloads.

High-level Redwood comparisons (ballpark, lanes for testing):
- Redwood hosted (recommended config): per-1M tokens estimate $55–$70 depending on batching and KV cache hit. Assumption: mixed prompt/response ratio ~ 1:4, avg seq length 1.5k tokens, 95th p99 latency SLO 350ms.
- Hyperscaler A (public endpoint): vendor quote implies $85–$110 per-1M under similar sequence assumptions due to lower batching efficiency and higher infra overhead for our workload profile.
- EdgeServe (small provider): $45–$60 per-1M but with limited SLOs and no prefix/KV caching; observed tail latency spikes on long contexts.

Important caveat: these numbers are highly sensitive to two operational levers: batch size distribution and prefix/KV cache hit rate. That drives effective tokens/sec on the GPU and net per-token cost.

Proposed empirical test matrix (minimal, 7-day window):
1) 1M-token synthetic run (single-threaded script + recorded traffic replay) per model variant: rwd-3b-q and rwd-13b-amt. Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU-hours, and raw cost.
2) Batching sweep: run the same 1M tokens with three steady-state batching profiles: immediate (batch=1), conservative batching (target 32), aggressive batching (target 128).
3) Cache warm/cold cycles: measure effective cost at 0% / 50% / 90% KV prefix cache hit rates (simulate by replaying traces with warm prefixes).
4) End-to-end comparison: run identical replay against a hyperscaler endpoint and EdgeServe (if they provide a short trial). Capture the same metrics and a token-level cost breakdown.

Deliverables we’ll share after the run: per-test CSVs, a pivoted cost model (cost/1M tokens with assumptions), and an exec-readout slide (single page).

Attachments: blueharbor-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), cost-model-worksheet.xlsx (editable assumptions), demo-screenshots.png (UI flows you asked about).

If that plan looks good I recommend we kick off tests next week — timeline below and proposed owners.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Kickoff and infra prep (Marcus) — provision dedicated short-lived test run capacity, set up replay harness. Goal: start Oct 23.
- Bench scripts and instrumentation (Aditya) — adapt your recorded traces and instrument p99/p95. Goal: Oct 22.
- Procurement checkpoint (Emily) — confirm trial endpoints for EdgeServe/hyperscaler, and share any contract constraints by Oct 21.

Let me know any changes you want to the matrix — we can tighten to fewer configs if you want a quicker delta.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0149

From: Emily Schultz <emily.schultz@blueharbor.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor follow-up: comparative econ recap + proposed test matrix

Marcus —

Appreciate the recap and the clear test plan. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 1.5k avg seq length you used matches our internal telemetry on summarization but our chat flows skew shorter (~600 tokens). Can we run the same matrix for both profile shapes?
- For hyperscaler A, we can provision a short trial endpoint via our cloud account but need to limit daily spend to $2k for the proof of concept; they'll throttle if exceeded.
- EdgeServe is willing to provide a 72-hour trial for our team with a maximum of 500k tokens.

Procurement note: I looped in procurement@blueharbor.ai to start the trial paperwork. We should get a green light for the hyperscaler trial by COB Monday.

Small ask: when you produce the CSVs, could you include a column that calculates effective cost per-1M tokens under our two profile shapes (chat: 600 tokens avg, summary: 1.5k avg)? That will make internal comparisons simpler.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Schultz
Head of Platform, BlueHarbor Analytics
emily.schultz@blueharbor.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Emily Schultz <emily.schultz@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Oct 2028 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor follow-up: comparative econ recap + proposed test matrix

Emily and team —

Thanks for the quick reply; happy to include both profile shapes. A couple of methodological notes so the comparison is apples-to-apples: 
- We'll normalize for model family (same FP16/quantization level) and sequence-length truncation. For the 600-token chat profile we expect higher tokens/sec but also lower batching headroom per request.
- Cost normalization: our run will record GPU-seconds and transform to $/1M tokens using Redwood's internal unit rates (we'll also show a normalized column that factors in your public hyperscaler bill rates so you can compare directly).

Proposed minimal test adjustments: 
- Add a shorter 600-token profile for each model in the matrix (so 2 sequence profiles x 2 models x 3 batching configs x 3 cache states). It increases run permutations, but we can stagger and parallelize.
- If EdgeServe restricts to 500k, we can still include them for the shorter chat profile and extrapolate cautiously for the 1.5k profile (we'll annotate extrapolation assumptions).

I've attached the cost-model-worksheet.xlsx with columns prefilled for the two profiles — Marcus, can you provision the test harness and share the Drive link we should push results to?

-Aditya

Aditya Rao
Lead Benchmarking Engineer, Redwood Inference
